from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Ant's Dilemma: Introduction to Dimensional Constraints"
        lines = [
            'Meet our ant, trapped inside a 2D circle.',
            'To the ant, the boundary is an impassable wall.',
            'A third dimension offers a path over it.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Define 2D elements
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color="#FF0000")
        self.place_in_area(circle, "B2", "E5")
        
        ant = Dot(color="#00FF00", radius=0.15)
        ant.move_to(circle.get_center())
        
        ant_label = Text("Ant", font_size=18, color="#00FF00")
        ant_label.next_to(ant, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(circle))
        self.play(FadeIn(ant), FadeIn(ant_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Ant moves to edge and shakes
        edge_point = circle.get_right()
        self.play(
            ant.animate.move_to(edge_point),
            ant_label.animate.next_to(edge_point, UP, buff=0.1)
        )
        
        # Shake to show it's stuck
        self.play(Wiggle(ant, scale_value=1.5), Wiggle(ant_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Z-axis arrow
        z_arrow = Arrow(
            start=LEFT * 0.5 + DOWN * 0.5,
            end=RIGHT * 0.5 + UP * 0.5,
            color="#0000FF",
            buff=0
        )
        self.place_at_grid(z_arrow, "B5")
        z_label = Text("Z-axis", font_size=16, color="#0000FF").next_to(z_arrow, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(z_arrow), FadeIn(z_label))
        
        # The 'Jump'
        # 1. Scale up and move diagonally 'up' (visually)
        jump_peak = circle.get_right() + UP * 1.0 + RIGHT * 0.5
        jump_land = circle.get_right() + RIGHT * 1.2
        
        self.play(
            ant.animate.scale(1.5).move_to(jump_peak),
            ant_label.animate.scale(1.5).next_to(jump_peak, UP, buff=0.1),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        # 2. Scale back and settle outside
        self.play(
            ant.animate.scale(1/1.5).move_to(jump_land),
            ant_label.animate.scale(1/1.5).next_to(jump_land, UP, buff=0.1),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Layout
        lines = [
            'A zero-dimensional point has position but no size.', 
            'Extending it creates a one-dimensional line segment.', 
            'Shifting the line sideways forms a 2D square.', 
            'Lifting the square creates a 3D cube.', 
            'Each step adds a new direction of freedom.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Knowledge: The 0D to 3D Ladder", lines)
        
        # Define common positions
        center_area = ('B2', 'E5')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        point = Dot(color="#FFFFFF", radius=0.08)
        label_0d = Text("0D: Point", font_size=20, color="#FFFFFF")
        
        self.place_in_area(point, *center_area)
        label_0d.next_to(point, DOWN, buff=0.3)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(point), Write(label_0d))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        cyan_line = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color="#00FFFF").scale(1.5)
        self.place_in_area(cyan_line, *center_area)
        label_1d = Text("1D", font_size=20, color="#00FFFF")
        label_1d.next_to(cyan_line, DOWN, buff=0.3)
        
        # Transition: Point expands to Line
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(point, cyan_line),
            ReplacementTransform(label_0d, label_1d)
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        yellow_square = Square(side_length=2.5, color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(yellow_square, *center_area)
        label_2d = Text("2D", font_size=20, color="#FFFF00")
        label_2d.next_to(yellow_square, DOWN, buff=0.3)
        
        # Transition: Line shifts to Square
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(cyan_line, yellow_square),
            ReplacementTransform(label_1d, label_2d)
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FF00FF")
        
        # Create Isometric Cube manually (Front, Back, and Edges)
        cube_color = "#FF00FF"
        size = 2.0
        offset = np.array([0.7, 0.7, 0])
        
        front_face = Square(side_length=size, color=cube_color, fill_opacity=0.1)
        back_face = Square(side_length=size, color=cube_color, fill_opacity=0.1).shift(offset)
        
        v_f = front_face.get_vertices()
        v_b = back_face.get_vertices()
        edges = VGroup(*[Line(v_f[i], v_b[i], color=cube_color) for i in range(4)])
        
        magenta_cube = VGroup(back_face, edges, front_face)
        self.place_in_area(magenta_cube, *center_area)
        
        label_3d = Text("3D: Space", font_size=20, color="#FF00FF")
        label_3d.next_to(magenta_cube, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        # Transition: Square lifts to Cube
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(yellow_square, magenta_cube),
            ReplacementTransform(label_2d, label_3d)
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Use Green for freedom highlight
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # Visualizing "freedom" with axes
        origin = magenta_cube.get_center() + LEFT*0.5 + DOWN*0.5
        x_axis = Arrow(origin, origin + RIGHT*1.5, color="#00FFFF", buff=0)
        y_axis = Arrow(origin, origin + UP*1.5, color="#FFFF00", buff=0)
        z_axis = Arrow(origin, origin + offset*1.5, color="#FF00FF", buff=0)
        
        axes = VGroup(x_axis, y_axis, z_axis)
        
        self.play(Create(axes))
        self.play(Indicate(axes, color="#00FF00"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        lecture_lines = [
            'Can six matchsticks form four equilateral triangles?',
            'In a flat plane, this puzzle seems impossible.',
            'Think outside the second dimension for the answer.',
            'Lifting the sticks creates a 3D tetrahedron.',
            'Shifting dimensions makes the impossible possible.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Puzzle 1: The Matchstick Triangle (The 2D to 3D Leap)", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        STICK_BROWN = "#A52A2A"
        TRI_YELLOW = "#FFFF00"
        FACE_GOLD = "#FFD700"

        # Coordinates for vertices relative to center
        # Center will be D4
        center_point = self.grid["D4"]
        
        # 2D Flat Triangle Vertices (Regular)
        s = 1.2 # side length
        v0_2d = center_point + np.array([0, s/np.sqrt(3), 0])
        v1_2d = center_point + np.array([-s/2, -s/(2*np.sqrt(3)), 0])
        v2_2d = center_point + np.array([s/2, -s/(2*np.sqrt(3)), 0])

        # 3D Projected Vertices (Squashed base + Apex)
        v0_3d = center_point + np.array([0, -0.4, 0])
        v1_3d = center_point + np.array([-0.8, -0.8, 0])
        v2_3d = center_point + np.array([0.8, -0.8, 0])
        v_apex = center_point + np.array([0, 0.8, 0])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Can six matchsticks form four equilateral triangles?
        self.lecture[0].set_color(STICK_BROWN)
        
        # Create 6 scattered sticks
        sticks = VGroup()
        scatter_points = ["B3", "C5", "E3", "F5", "B6", "E2"]
        for pos in scatter_points:
            stick = Line(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 0.8, color=STICK_BROWN, stroke_width=6)
            stick.rotate(np.random.rand() * PI)
            self.place_at_grid(stick, pos)
            sticks.add(stick)
            
        self.play(LaggedStartMap(Create, sticks, lag_ratio=0.2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # In a flat plane, this puzzle seems impossible.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(TRI_YELLOW)
        
        # Move 3 sticks to form a base triangle
        self.play(
            sticks[0].animate.put_start_and_end_on(v1_2d, v2_2d).set_color(TRI_YELLOW),
            sticks[1].animate.put_start_and_end_on(v2_2d, v0_2d).set_color(TRI_YELLOW),
            sticks[2].animate.put_start_and_end_on(v0_2d, v1_2d).set_color(TRI_YELLOW),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Think outside the second dimension for the answer.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(STICK_BROWN)
        
        # Move other 3 sticks to "failed" 2D positions (overlapping/stretching)
        # Attempting to make more triangles in 2D
        v_fail = center_point + np.array([0, -s*1.2, 0])
        self.play(
            sticks[3].animate.put_start_and_end_on(v1_2d, v_fail),
            sticks[4].animate.put_start_and_end_on(v2_2d, v_fail),
            sticks[5].animate.put_start_and_end_on(v0_2d, center_point + np.array([s*0.8, s*0.8, 0])),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Lifting the sticks creates a 3D tetrahedron.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(FACE_GOLD)
        
        # Transition to "3D" isometric view
        # We transform all 6 sticks to form the tetrahedron
        self.play(
            # Base triangle squashes
            sticks[0].animate.put_start_and_end_on(v1_3d, v2_3d).set_color(TRI_YELLOW),
            sticks[1].animate.put_start_and_end_on(v2_3d, v0_3d).set_color(TRI_YELLOW),
            sticks[2].animate.put_start_and_end_on(v0_3d, v1_3d).set_color(TRI_YELLOW),
            # Lift the other three
            sticks[3].animate.put_start_and_end_on(v1_3d, v_apex).set_color(STICK_BROWN),
            sticks[4].animate.put_start_and_end_on(v2_3d, v_apex).set_color(STICK_BROWN),
            sticks[5].animate.put_start_and_end_on(v0_3d, v_apex).set_color(STICK_BROWN),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Shifting dimensions makes the impossible possible.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(FACE_GOLD)
        
        # Highlight faces and add numbers
        face_base = Polygon(v0_3d, v1_3d, v2_3d, fill_opacity=0.3, fill_color=FACE_GOLD, stroke_width=0)
        face_left = Polygon(v1_3d, v0_3d, v_apex, fill_opacity=0.4, fill_color=FACE_GOLD, stroke_width=0)
        face_right = Polygon(v2_3d, v0_3d, v_apex, fill_opacity=0.2, fill_color=FACE_GOLD, stroke_width=0)
        face_front = Polygon(v1_3d, v2_3d, v_apex, fill_opacity=0.5, fill_color=FACE_GOLD, stroke_width=0)

        faces = VGroup(face_base, face_left, face_right, face_front)
        
        # Face numbers (placed near face centroids)
        c_base = (v0_3d + v1_3d + v2_3d) / 3 + DOWN * 0.1
        c_left = (v1_3d + v0_3d + v_apex) / 3
        c_right = (v2_3d + v0_3d + v_apex) / 3
        c_front = (v1_3d + v2_3d + v_apex) / 3

        num1 = Text("1", font_size=24).move_to(c_base)
        num2 = Text("2", font_size=24).move_to(c_left)
        num3 = Text("3", font_size=24).move_to(c_right)
        num4 = Text("4", font_size=24).move_to(c_front)
        nums = VGroup(num1, num2, num3, num4)

        self.play(FadeIn(faces), FadeIn(nums))
        self.play(
            faces.animate.set_fill(FACE_GOLD, opacity=0.6),
            nums.animate.scale(1.2),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and Lecture Lines
        lecture_lines = [
            'Finding the shortest path on a cube is tricky.',
            'A spider must reach an opposite corner.',
            "Unfold the cube's surfaces into a flat net.",
            'Now, the shortest path is a straight line.',
            'Folding back reveals the optimal 3D route.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The 'Unfolding' Technique: 3D to 2D Projection", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        CUBE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        NET_COLOR = "#D3D3D3"
        SPIDER_COLOR = "#FF0000"
        FLY_COLOR = "#0000FF"
        PATH_COLOR = "#00FF00"

        # Model Space helper: Simple Isometric Projection
        def iso(x, y, z):
            # Projects 3D (x,y,z) to 2D (x', y')
            return np.array([(x - z) * 1.0, y + (x + z) * 0.5, 0])

        # Grid area configuration
        grid_center = (self.grid["A1"] + self.grid["F6"]) / 2
        scale_val = 1.0

        # Geometry Data
        # Vertices of a 1x1x1 cube centered at origin
        pts_3d = [
            [-0.5, -0.5, -0.5], [ 0.5, -0.5, -0.5], [ 0.5,  0.5, -0.5], [-0.5,  0.5, -0.5],
            [-0.5, -0.5,  0.5], [ 0.5, -0.5,  0.5], [ 0.5,  0.5,  0.5], [-0.5,  0.5,  0.5]
        ]
        face_names = ["Front", "Top", "Bottom", "Left", "Right", "Back"]
        face_indices = {
            "Front": [4, 5, 6, 7], "Top": [7, 6, 2, 3], "Bottom": [0, 1, 5, 4],
            "Left": [0, 4, 7, 3], "Right": [5, 1, 2, 6], "Back": [1, 0, 3, 2]
        }
        # T-shape net coordinates (relative to Front at 0,0)
        face_net_coords = {
            "Front":  [[-0.5,-0.5], [ 0.5,-0.5], [ 0.5, 0.5], [-0.5, 0.5]],
            "Top":    [[-0.5, 0.5], [ 0.5, 0.5], [ 0.5, 1.5], [-0.5, 1.5]],
            "Bottom": [[-0.5,-1.5], [ 0.5,-1.5], [ 0.5,-0.5], [-0.5,-0.5]],
            "Left":   [[-1.5,-0.5], [-0.5,-0.5], [-0.5, 0.5], [-1.5, 0.5]],
            "Right":  [[ 0.5,-0.5], [ 1.5,-0.5], [ 1.5, 0.5], [ 0.5, 0.5]],
            "Back":   [[-0.5,-2.5], [ 0.5,-2.5], [ 0.5,-1.5], [-0.5,-1.5]]
        }

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create Isometric Cube Faces
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        faces = VGroup()
        face_dict = {}
        for name in face_names:
            poly = Polygon(*[iso(*pts_3d[i]) * scale_val + grid_center for i in face_indices[name]], 
                           stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=2, fill_color=CUBE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.4)
            face_dict[name] = poly
            faces.add(poly)

        self.play(FadeIn(faces))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Spider at P7 (Top-Front-Left), Fly at P1 (Bottom-Back-Right)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        spider_start = iso(*pts_3d[7]) * scale_val + grid_center
        fly_start = iso(*pts_3d[1]) * scale_val + grid_center
        
        spider = Dot(spider_start, color=SPIDER_COLOR, radius=0.12)
        fly = Dot(fly_start, color=FLY_COLOR, radius=0.12)
        spider_label = Text("Spider", font_size=16, color=SPIDER_COLOR).next_to(spider, UP, buff=0.1)
        fly_label = Text("Fly", font_size=16, color=FLY_COLOR).next_to(fly, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        self.play(FadeIn(spider), FadeIn(fly), Write(spider_label), Write(fly_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Unfold Cube to T-shape Net
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        net_offset = np.array([0, 0.5, 0]) * scale_val # Center the 4-unit high net
        
        unfold_anims = []
        for name in face_names:
            target_pts = [np.array([c[0], c[1], 0]) * scale_val + grid_center + net_offset for c in face_net_coords[name]]
            unfold_anims.append(face_dict[name].animate.become(
                Polygon(*target_pts, fill_color=NET_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
            ))
            
        # P7 is top-left of Front face in net: (-0.5, 0.5)
        # P1 is bottom-right of Right face in net: (1.5, -0.5)
        spider_target = np.array([-0.5, 0.5, 0]) * scale_val + grid_center + net_offset
        fly_target = np.array([1.5, -0.5, 0]) * scale_val + grid_center + net_offset
        
        self.play(
            *unfold_anims, 
            spider.animate.move_to(spider_target),
            fly.animate.move_to(fly_target),
            spider_label.animate.next_to(spider_target, UP, buff=0.1),
            fly_label.animate.next_to(fly_target, DOWN, buff=0.1),
            run_time=2.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Draw shortest path as straight line on net
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        path_line = Line(spider_target, fly_target, color=PATH_COLOR, stroke_width=5)
        self.play(Create(path_line))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Fold back to cube showing the segmented shortest path
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Calculate segmented path in 3D: P7 -> Edge Center -> P1
        # Intersection on Front-Right edge at (0.5, 0, 0.5)
        mid_pt_3d = [0.5, 0, 0.5]
        mid_pt_scene = iso(*mid_pt_3d) * scale_val + grid_center
        
        path_3d = VGroup(
            Line(spider_start, mid_pt_scene, color=PATH_COLOR, stroke_width=5),
            Line(mid_pt_scene, fly_start, color=PATH_COLOR, stroke_width=5)
        )
        
        fold_anims = []
        for name in face_names:
            orig_pts = [iso(*pts_3d[i]) * scale_val + grid_center for i in face_indices[name]]
            fold_anims.append(face_dict[name].animate.become(
                Polygon(*orig_pts, fill_color=CUBE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.4, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
            ))

        self.play(
            *fold_anims,
            spider.animate.move_to(spider_start),
            fly.animate.move_to(fly_start),
            spider_label.animate.next_to(spider_start, UP, buff=0.1),
            fly_label.animate.next_to(fly_start, DOWN, buff=0.1),
            ReplacementTransform(path_line, path_3d),
            run_time=2.5
        )
        self.wait(3)

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize the scene layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "Topology Twist: The Möbius Strip", 
            [
                'Take a strip of paper and twist it.', 
                'This Möbius strip has one side and one edge.', 
                'Moving along it flips perspective without crossing edges.'
            ]
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create a white rectangular strip
        strip = Rectangle(
            width=4.0, height=0.6, 
            color="#FFFFFF", 
            fill_color="#FFFFFF", 
            fill_opacity=1.0,
            stroke_width=2
        )
        self.place_in_area(strip, "B2", "E5")
        
        # Initial lecture line color
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(Create(strip))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Create a "twisted" version of the strip (narrows in center)
        # Using a polygon to simulate the 180-degree twist in 2D
        w = 2.0
        h = 0.3
        twisted_points = [
            strip.get_corner(UL), 
            strip.get_edge_center(UP) + DOWN * 0.25, # dip in middle
            strip.get_corner(UR),
            strip.get_corner(DR),
            strip.get_edge_center(DOWN) + UP * 0.25, # rise in middle
            strip.get_corner(DL)
        ]
        twisted_strip = Polygon(
            *twisted_points, 
            color="#FFFFFF", 
            fill_opacity=1.0,
            stroke_width=2
        )
        # Add shading effect in the middle
        twisted_strip.set_fill(color=["#FFFFFF", "#888888", "#FFFFFF"])
        
        self.play(Transform(strip, twisted_strip))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Create the blue Möbius loop (using a lemniscate shape as a 2D projection)
        mobius_path = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([
                2.2 * np.cos(t),
                1.0 * np.sin(2 * t),
                0
            ]),
            t_range=[0, TAU],
            color="#00BFFF"
        )
        
        # Make the loop visually distinct as a "strip" by giving it width
        mobius_loop_visual = mobius_path.copy().set_stroke(width=16)
        self.place_in_area(mobius_loop_visual, "B1", "E6")
        
        # Sync the path used for animation with the scaled visual object
        mobius_path.match_points(mobius_loop_visual)

        self.play(
            Transform(strip, mobius_loop_visual),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00BFFF"),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Orange dot traversing the loop
        dot = Dot(color="#FF4500", radius=0.15)
        dot.move_to(mobius_path.get_start())
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.play(FadeIn(dot))
        
        # Traverse the loop
        # On a figure-eight path, this visits "both" loops of the 8, 
        # representing the traversal of both sides of the twist
        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(dot, mobius_path),
            run_time=5,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        
        self.play(FadeOut(dot))
        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        lines = [
            'When stuck, look for a higher dimension.',
            'Dimensional shifts solve problems where flat logic fails.',
            'Master the shift to see beyond constraints.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary: The 'N+1' Mindset", lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a tangled yellow loop (#FFD700) representing a knot constrained to 2D.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create a self-intersecting "knot" in 2D
        # Using a figure-eight style path that overlaps
        knot_points = [
            [0, 0, 0], [1, 1, 0], [0, 2, 0], [-1, 1, 0], 
            [1, -1, 0], [0, -2, 0], [-1, -1, 0], [0, 0, 0]
        ]
        tangled_loop = VMobject()
        tangled_loop.set_points_as_corners(knot_points)
        tangled_loop.set_smooth_curve(True)
        tangled_loop.set_color("#FFD700") # Gold
        
        self.place_in_area(tangled_loop, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(tangled_loop), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # A cross-over point flashes white (#FFFFFF) as one segment lifts 'up' 
        # into the 3rd dimension to clear the other.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Intersection point for the flash (center of the knot)
        flash_dot = Dot(color="#FFFFFF").move_to(tangled_loop.get_center())
        
        # Create a "lifted" version of the loop (broken at intersection to look like it passed over)
        # We simulate the "lifting" by starting to untie it.
        untied_path = Circle(radius=1.5, color="#FFD700")
        self.place_in_area(untied_path, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(Flash(flash_dot, color="#FFFFFF", line_length=0.3, flash_radius=0.5, num_lines=12))
        self.play(
            tangled_loop.animate.become(untied_path),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=slow_into
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The knot unties into a green circle (#00FF00) with the text 'N+1: A New Perspective' (#FFFFFF).
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        final_circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_in_area(final_circle, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        perspective_text = Text("N+1: A New Perspective", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF")
        # Position text inside or near the circle
        self.place_at_grid(perspective_text, "C3", scale_factor=0.7)
        perspective_text.next_to(final_circle, DOWN, buff=0.3)

        self.play(
            Transform(tangled_loop, final_circle),
            Write(perspective_text),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: The Art of Dimensional Shifting: Geometry Beyond the Flat
outline.target_audience: High school students and geometry enthusiasts

sections.title: The Ant's Dilemma: Introduction to Dimensional Constraints
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a 'dimension' as a constraint on movement. Use a narrative hook where a character is trapped in a lower-dimensional world to spark curiosity about 'escaping' through a higher dimension.
sections.example: An ant (2D traveler) is trapped inside a circle drawn on paper. It cannot cross the line. To escape, it must understand the 3rd dimension (Z-axis) to 'jump' over the line, a concept it can't initially perceive.

sections.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: The 0D to 3D Ladder
sections.content: Establish the foundational vocabulary. Define Point (0D), Line (1D), Plane (2D), and Space (3D) using a coordinate system (x, y, z) to ensure students understand the mathematical 'freedom' added by each axis.
sections.example: Visualizing a point stretching into a line segment, the line sliding to form a square, and the square lifting upward to form a transparent cube.

sections.title: Puzzle 1: The Matchstick Triangle (The 2D to 3D Leap)
sections.content: Present a classic geometry puzzle that seems impossible in 2D. This teaches students to question the 'implied' dimensions of a problem statement.
sections.example: Task: Use 6 identical matchsticks to form 4 equilateral triangles. In 2D, this is impossible. Solution: Shift to 3D to build a tetrahedron (a triangular pyramid).

sections.title: The 'Unfolding' Technique: 3D to 2D Projection
sections.content: Teach the reverse skill: solving 3D pathfinding problems by flattening them into 2D 'nets.' This is critical for calculating shortest distances on complex surfaces.
sections.example: A spider is at one corner of a cube and needs to reach a fly at the opposite corner. Instead of guessing the diagonal, we 'unfold' the cube into a flat T-shape (net) and draw a straight line between the two points.

sections.title: Topology Twist: The Möbius Strip
sections.content: Introduce the concept of non-orientable surfaces where a 2D plane is twisted through 3D space to create a one-sided object. This challenges the definition of 'inside' and 'outside.'
sections.example: A paper loop with a 180-degree twist. If a '2D car' drives along it, it will eventually return to the start point having traveled both 'sides' without ever crossing an edge.

sections.title: Summary: The 'N+1' Mindset
sections.content: Conclude by reinforcing the rule: When a problem is unsolvable in 'N' dimensions, look for a solution in 'N+1.' Summarize how dimensional shifts are used in modern tech like GPS and data folding.
sections.example: Comparison animation: A tangled knot in a 2D string that can only be untied by lifting a loop into the 3rd dimension, showing that 'impossible' is often just a 'lack of perspective.'

storyboard.title: The Ant's Dilemma: Introduction to Dimensional Constraints
lecture_lines: Meet our ant, trapped inside a flat 2D circle.
To the ant, this boundary is an impassable wall.
But a new axis offers a path through height.
The ant leaps over the once-solid barrier.
It lands safely on the other side.
animations: Show a 2D plane with a red circle (#FF0000) and an ant [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ant.svg] inside.
The ant [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ant.svg] moves to the circle edge, stops, and shakes to show it's stuck.
A blue arrow (#0000FF) tilted at 45 degrees appears to represent the Z-axis (height).
The ant [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ant.svg] scales up 1.5x and moves diagonally 'up and over' the circle line.
The ant [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ant.svg] scales back to 1.0x and settles on the plane outside the circle.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: The 0D to 3D Ladder
lecture_lines: A zero-dimensional point marks a single location.
Stretching it creates lines, then flat 2D shapes.
Shifting into 3D transforms the square into a cube.
animations: A white point [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/point.svg] (#FFFFFF) appears in the center, labeled '0D: Point'.
The point stretches horizontally into a cyan line (#00FFFF) '1D', then vertically into a yellow square (#FFFF00) '2D'.
The square stretches diagonally into an isometric magenta cube (#FF00FF) labeled '3D: Space'.

storyboard.title: Puzzle 1: The Matchstick Triangle (The 2D to 3D Leap)
lecture_lines: Can six matchsticks form four equilateral triangles?
We can easily build one triangle in 2D.
But the remaining sticks fail to form more.
Lift the sticks into the third dimension instead.
Now, a 3D tetrahedron creates four perfect triangles.
animations: Six brown matchstick segments (#A52A2A) are scattered randomly on the screen.
Three segments form a single flat yellow triangle (#FFFF00) in the center.
The other three segments try to form triangles on the plane but overlap and fail.
The three segments lift and connect to a single point above the first triangle (isometric view).
The resulting 3D tetrahedron's four faces are highlighted in gold (#FFD700) and numbered 1-4.

storyboard.title: The 'Unfolding' Technique: 3D to 2D Projection
lecture_lines: Finding the shortest path across a cube is tricky.
Unfold the 3D surface into a flat 2D net.
Now, a simple straight line reveals the best route.
animations: Display a white isometric cube (#FFFFFF) with a red dot 'Spider' (#FF0000) and blue dot 'Fly' (#0000FF) at opposite corners.
The cube faces rotate and flatten out into a light grey 2D 'T-shape' net (#D3D3D3).
A straight green line (#00FF00) is drawn between the red and blue dots on the flat net.

storyboard.title: Topology Twist: The Möbius Strip
lecture_lines: Start with a simple, flat rectangular strip.
Add a half-twist to the center of the strip.
Joining the ends creates the famous Möbius loop.
Follow the path along its single continuous surface.
One journey visits both sides without crossing an edge.
animations: Show a long, flat white rectangular strip (#FFFFFF) [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/strip.svg].
The strip's middle section narrows and changes shading to represent a 180-degree twist.
The ends of the twisted strip connect to form a blue Möbius loop (#00BFFF).
An orange dot (#FF4500) begins a slow traversal along the center of the Möbius loop.
The dot completes one full cycle, visiting what were both 'sides' before returning to start.

storyboard.title: Summary: The 'N+1' Mindset
lecture_lines: A 2D knot seems impossible to untie.
Lifting a loop into 3D releases the constraint.
Solve complex problems by seeking the next dimension.
animations: Show a tangled yellow loop (#FFD700) representing a knot [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/knot.svg] constrained to 2D.
A cross-over point flashes white (#FFFFFF) as one segment lifts 'up' into the 3rd dimension to clear the other.
The knot unties into a green circle (#00FF00) [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/loop.svg] with the text 'N+1: A New Perspective' (#FFFFFF).
